messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED @sre-oncall (Priya) - high 95p latency + error spike on hosted-inference across ml-prod pools for Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants. Alerts show KV cache growth + continuous-batching backlog.
Priya: I'm on it. seeing 5xx rate climb and token latency up ~3-4x. queue depth looks correlated with long prefix reuse.
Marco: adding context — noticed anomalous KV write amplification on nodes serving MQA config. eviction rate dropped to near zero, mem use trending to 98%.
Ben: rolling up logs: heatmap shows many small requests grouping into large batched frames, batch_size_max=64 pushed by a recent rollout. Could be batch jitter + MQA causing oversized KV entries.
Alice: support already getting customer pings about timeouts. ETA on mitigation? need a customer impact estimate for SRE->Sales sync.
Priya: immediate plan: 1) throttle acceptance on affected routings (set concurrency cap), 2) apply emergency batch_size_max=16 hotpatch, 3) bump eviction aggressiveness (kv.eviction_hysteresis=0.6 -> 0.4). Marco can apply steps 2+3?
Marco: will push config hotfix to prod pool A,B,C. doing canary on pool-A first. deploy-bot: starting canary rollout 1/5 nodes with config change: batch_size_max=16, kv.eviction_threshold=0.6 -> 0.45.
Ben: also propose temporary model-routing to fallback quantized variants for Llama/Mistral where possible to reduce KV footprint. That requires route table tweak.
Priya: agree. set strict-route for high-traffic customers to qwen-quantized-v2 and mistral-q8 fallback. We want to avoid cross-model prefetches until stable.
deploy-bot: canary applied to pool-A at 3612345840. metrics: tail latency down 25% on canary nodes, kv mem dropping from 96% -> 84%.
inc-bot: Incident severity -> Sev2. Tagging incident-owner: Priya.
Marco: applying full hotpatch to pool-B/C now. pushing script: 
```
./apply_hotpatch --pool pool-B --set batch_size_max=16 --set kv.eviction_hysteresis=0.45 --restart-infer-worker
```
Priya: while Marco patches, I'm throttling incoming routing rules for non-prod tokens and applying a temporary per-tenant qps cap on the largest customers to avoid cascading prefetch.
Alice: support note drafted and queued to send to impacted customers: short summary + mitigation steps + ETA for root cause. Will hold until we confirm impact numbers.
Ben: quick analysis: root cause hypothesis: a recent change to dynamic-batching heuristics increased aggression for short-prefix sessions. For MQA/GQA, that led to large batches with high prefix overlap; KV entries grew superlinearly because we store combined key blobs for merged prefetched segments. On Qwen, a separate codepath for async prefetch created duplicate writes.
Priya: Good summary. Action items: 1) hotpatch rollout (in progress), 2) enforce batch_size ceiling at router for 2h, 3) disable async prefetch for Qwen, 4) customer notifications, 5) post-incident evals and regression test for MQA/GQA batches.
Marco: disabling async prefetch for Qwen now via feature-flag: feature/qwen-async-prefetch=false. deploy-bot: flag flip at 3612346000 successful.
deploy-bot: full hotpatch completed 3612346100 across pools. Telemetry: global 95p latency back to baseline, 5xxs reduced to normal. KV mem usage trending down.
Priya: initiating targeted paging to oncall infra to verify shard stabilization overnight. Also scheduling rollback window if any negative perf regressions.
Alice: sending initial customer comms now: message includes affected models list (llama-2x, mistral-7b-v2, qwen-7b-mixed), mitigation we applied, and expected follow-up. support-bot: queued email to customers at 3612346200.
support-bot: dispatched to 12 customers that reported timeouts; copy posted to #customer-status.
Ben: for postmortem: need to revert the dynamic-batching heuristic change, add gating by model-family (MQA/GQA sensitive), and add a canary test that simulates high prefix-cardinality traffic to verify KV stability.
Marco: also recommend adding a soft-limit on combined-kv-entry-size and an eviction override if mem > 90% for 30s. that'll prevent runaway growth while we root cause.
Priya: logging these items. Initial impact: estimated 10% of hosted inference customers saw elevated latency/timeouts over 18m window, 3 direct P1 customer reports. No data loss.
Alice: coordinating customer follow-ups — will escalate to AMs for affected enterprise customers.
Priya: incident status: mitigated at 3612346100, monitoring for 30m. assigning postmortem owners: Ben (root cause + repro), Marco (hotpatch docs + runbook update), Alice (customer comms + timeline).
inc-bot: Incident closed to monitoring at 3612346400.
Priya: quick note — when we do the postmortem, include load profiles that distinguish continuous-batching vs single-shot requests; the failure surface was specifically the combination of aggressive batching + async prefetch duplicates on Qwen.
Alice: thanks everyone. I'll stitch the timeline for AMs and legal if needed. :thumbsup:
Marco: grabbing metrics snapshot and saving runbooks. Will follow up with a short PR to flag the heuristic behind a feature gate.
Ben: I'll add the KV entry size limiter and create e2e tests that replay the customer traffic we saw.
Priya: closing thread, will reopen if we see reoccurrence.
